name: Spider Curl
description: The spider curl is performed lying face-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging vertically, so the elbows are in front of the body throughout the range of motion. This position eliminates momentum from body swing and keeps the biceps under tension at both the stretched and contracted positions. With the shoulder in some extension, the long head of the biceps is under greater tension during the curl compared to standard standing variations.

execution.starting_position: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-60 degree incline. Lie face-down on the bench with the chest resting on the pad and the arms hanging straight down, holding dumbbells (or a barbell) with a supinated grip.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the bench to approximately 45 degrees. Lie prone with the chest at the top edge of the pad. Arms hang straight down — the bench supports the chest, not the arms.
steps: Step 1: Lie face-down on the incline bench. Arms hang vertically with dumbbells in a supinated grip.
Step 2: The upper arms remain vertical and stationary — only the forearms move.
Step 3: Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward, bending only at the elbow until the biceps are fully contracted.
Step 4: Inhale and lower the dumbbells in a controlled motion back to full arm extension, feeling the stretch at the bottom.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl; inhale on the controlled lowering.
common_mistakes: Letting the upper arms swing backward during the curl — they must stay vertical
Using momentum by bouncing at the bottom of the range
safety_considerations: Do not hyperextend the elbows at the bottom
If anterior shoulder discomfort occurs, reduce the bench angle slightly
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow extension at the bottom; full bicep contraction at the top.
coaching_cues: Let your arms hang straight down like plumb lines — that is the start position
Feel the stretch at the bottom before curling — do not bounce out of it
